10. **Characters, first package: who they are.** "Errands, not roles", "Kings never see skills" (claims and checks) and "Seeing oneself" (characters who over- or underestimate themselves, and may come to doubt it), "A name made of outcomes" (reputation from what was seen to happen, so luck makes names), "Declaring a name" and false envoys, "A past before the game, then a past made in play", "What servants know" (the record of who saw what, and questioning a captive), "Attested characters" and "Nubians in Egypt's service". Captives can be exchanged between courts like any good. Tablets are taken, not only copied: a spy may be sent to steal a tablet from a court's archive, and a conqueror carries off the archive of a capital he takes, so that its court loses it ("Tablets have a place", "Tablets are objects in a place"). A larger starting pool: with errands widening what characters do, 18 characters are too few to staff seven courts (each power starts with two envoys, leaving four free agents for everything else), and a shortage would distort this item's own script-king benchmarks. Raise the starting pool to about 60 as a first guess under the balance rule, a setting of the table ("How many characters"), mostly ordinary people and few excellent ones ("Enough people, not enough good ones"). Each power still starts with two envoys; the rest are free agents. Draw the extra characters from their own seeded stream, so existing seeds keep their first 18. Item 11 makes the pool live, and item 18 tunes its size.
